PULMONARY EMBOLISM  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
RISK FACTORS FOR PE 
                  “THROMBOSIS” 
*Trauma/Travel 
*Hypercoagulable state/HRT 
*Recreational drugs (IVDU) 
*Older 
*Malignancy 
*Birth Control 
*Obesity/Obstetrical  
  (risk of PE is highest in the first 6 weeks postpartum) 
*Surgery 
*Immobilization 
*Sickness 
                      HISTORY 
*Chest pain 
*Shortness of breath 
*Palpitations 
*Haemoptysis 
*Syncope or pre-syncope 
*Unexplained fatigue / breathlessness 
*Gynae hx – pregnant / oestrogen-based contraception 
*Previous surgery or immobilization in the last 4 weeks 
*Previous DVT or PE 
*Malignancy 
*Travel history 
CLINICAL SIGNS AND SYMPTOMS 
*Non-specific 
*High index of suspicion especially in patients with 
 
-unexplained dyspnoea 
 
-tachypnoea 
 
-unexplained tachycardia 
 
-unilateral leg swelling 
INVESTIGATIONS 
BEDSIDE 
* ECG 
  - sinus tachycardia 
  - T wave inversions in the right praecordial leads (V1-V4) and inferior leads (II, III, avF) 
  - Non-specific ST-T wave abnormalities – STE or STD 
  - S1 Q3 T3  
  - Dominant R wave in V1 
  - Right ventricular enlargement – peaked p-wave in lead II > 2.5mm in height 
  - Right heart strain and acute cor pulmonale 
 
- tall peaked p-waves in lead II 
 
- right axis deviation 
 
- RBBB  
 
- S1Q3T3 
  - Atrial tachyarrhythmias 
 
-atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, atrial tachycardia 
  - May be completely normal  
 
* ABG 
  - hypoxaemia 
  - hypocapnia 
  - respiratory alkalosis 
 
* Point of Care Ultrasound (POCUS) 
  - Echo  
 
- RV enlargement 
 
- RV free wall hypokinesia 
 
- McConnell’s Sign – akinesia of the mid free wall with sparing of the RV apex 
 
- Interventricular septal flattening  
 
- Plethoric/dilated IVC 
  - LCUS – assessment for an acute proximal DVT in the lower limbs 
   
LABORATORY 
* U&E, FBC, CRP, D-dimer, Trop T 
 
RADIOLOGICAL 
*CXR 
  - may be normal 
  - Hamptons hump – wedge-shaped, pleural based triangular opacity with an apex      
    pointing toward the hilus 
  - Westermark sign – decreased vascularity with dilation of the pulmonary vessels and  
    sharp cutoff 
*CTPA = Gold standard 
Dr M Wu / Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020 
 
INDICATIONS FOR THROMBOLYSIS 
 
1. Massive PE 
*Sustained hypotension (SBP <  
   90mmHg) for 15 minutes or requiring    
   inotropic support 
*Persistent bradycardia with signs of  
   shock 
*RV dysfunction on echo 
*Myocardial necrosis  
   (Trop I > 0.4ng/ml or Trop T > 0.1ng/ml) 
 
2. Cardiac Arrest in PE 
AGE ADJUSTED D-DIMER 
THRESHOLD = AGE (>50 years) x 10 
TRIMESTER ADJUSTED 
 D-DIMER THRESHOLD 
 
1st - < 750 ng/ml (0.75mg/l) 
2nd - < 1000 ng/ml (1mg/l) 
3rd - < 1250 ng/ml (1.25mg/l) 
THROMBOLYTIC OF CHOICE 
ALTEPLASE (ACTILYSE®) 
 
1. Massive PE 
*≥65kg 
  10mg bolus followed by 90mg  
  infusion over 2 hours 
*<65kg 
  Total dose of 1.5mg/kg 
  10mg bolus and remainder of dose  
  infused over 2 hours 
 
2. Cardiac Arrest 
    50mg IVI as a stat dose
